chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him):

A woman came to him, and a man had married her and consummated the marriage with her, and he specified a dowry for her, and he specified a term for her dowry. So Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You have no term for her dowry if you have consummated the marriage with her, so pay her her right.'

key_terms.أَجَلاً: A specified term or period of time
key_terms.حَقَّهَا: Her right (referring to the full dowry)
key_terms.مَهْرًا: Dowry or bridal gift specified in marriage contract

ai.seo_question: What happens to a deferred dowry when the marriage is consummated?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS) clarifies that the stipulation of a deferred payment term for the dowry (mahr) is voided upon consummation of the marriage, making the full amount immediately due. This ruling underscores the principle that the husband's right to intimacy triggers the wife's immediate entitlement to her financial rights, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding conditional dowries. It highlights the legal transition from a deferred obligation to an immediate debt upon the fulfillment of the marital bond.
